The name Zulema is also associated with the Arabic name 'Zulayma', which means 'tender' or 'gentle'. In modern times, the name Zulema has been used in various Christian cultures, including Spanish-speaking countries, to signify a child born with a gentle soul. As a given name, Zulema is often associated with qualities such as compassion, empathy, and kindness.

She was said to have been the daughter of the last Moorish king of Granada, Boabdil, and was known for her exceptional beauty and wisdom. Her conversion was instrumental in the eventual Christian victory over the Moors.

Another legend tells of a Moorish princess named Zuleima, who was said to be the daughter of the last Moorish king of Seville, Abu Abd Allah, and was renowned for her beauty. According to the legend, she fell in love with a Christian knight named Fernán González, who was sent on a mission to Seville. Their love was forbidden by both the Christian and Muslim authorities, leading to a tragic ending.
